ceiling_directive: Close the factor-two logarithmic elbow by proving a compatible-prefix estimator variance bound and a matching legal-subtree testing converse, yielding explicit all-sample risk and honest-length rates.
improvement_directive: Construct the proposed joint prefix-polynomial or factorial-moment estimator with a nested-count covariance theorem, then match it with fixed-sample priors supported on legal subtrees. Use the resulting common scale to derive the complete consistency and known-propensity penalty phase diagram.
critique: The note proves a matched frontier only in the long-history regime T >= 2k_n, together with computable but unmatched upper and lower envelopes elsewhere; it does not prove the advertised sharp unknown-history frontier for all n,T,c. The intermediate logarithmic transition, exact uniform-consistency conditions, and exact characterization of when propensity knowledge changes the order all remain open in oeq:compatible-prefix-approximation and oeq:sharp-frontier. The TL;DR and project framing accurately limit the matched claim to long histories, but the title-level frontier contribution is therefore under-delivered relative to the stated research object. The long-history theorem, oracle comparison, and finite-depth bracket form a genuine specialized contribution, yet the unresolved regime prevents a field-tier paper and materially limits the projected journal score. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 5.5 < 7.2, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
